claims.reason: The first reviewer has the instance's name wrong: Mathlib has no `algebraInt`. The global instance is `Ring.toIntAlgebra : Algebra ℤ R` for any `[Ring R]` (Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Basic.lean:296). `int_algebra_subsingleton` does exist (line 308). Without the binder, `[CommRing A]` still supplies `Algebra ℤ A`, so `aeval (R := ℤ) a` elaborates and nothing else in the statement mentions the binder. The statement is still true and provable: it is the current theorem instantiated at `Ring.toIntAlgebra A`, so it follows from the existing proof applied to that instance. The proof (`hom_eval₂`, `congr 1`, `Polynomial.ringHom_ext'`, `RingHom.ext_int`, `simp`) is generic in the instance anyway. This is a plain deletion, not a weakening.

Same argument as for A. `[CommRing B]` supplies `Ring.toIntAlgebra B`, so `aeval (R := ℤ) (g a)` still elaborates. The binder appears nowhere else in the statement. The reduced theorem is a special case of the current one with the canonical instance, so it is still true and provable, whether this binder is deleted alone or together with `[Algebra ℤ A]`.
